title: एकोनविंशतितमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Krishna describes the rich city of Magadha guarded by its five hills. The three break the city's sacred drums, enter by a forbidden way, and appear before Jarasandha, who honours them as Brahmins but is suspicious; they declare that they take no hospitality from an enemy.
summary.kn: ಐದು ಬೆಟ್ಟಗಳು ಕಾಯುವ ಸಮೃದ್ಧ ಮಗಧ ನಗರವನ್ನು ಶ್ರೀಕೃಷ್ಣನು ವರ್ಣಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಮೂವರೂ ನಗರದ ಪವಿತ್ರ ಭೇರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಒಡೆದು ನಿಷಿದ್ಧ ದಾರಿಯಿಂದ ಪ್ರವೇಶಿಸಿ ಜರಾಸಂಧನ ಮುಂದೆ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರೆಂದು ಸತ್ಕರಿಸಿದರೂ ಅವನು ಶಂಕಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಶತ್ರುವಿನ ಆತಿಥ್ಯ ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸೆವು ಎಂದು ಅವರು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: श्रीकृष्ण पाँच पहाड़ियों से रक्षित मगध की समृद्ध नगरी का वर्णन करते हैं। तीनों नगर के पवित्र नगाड़े तोड़कर वर्जित मार्ग से प्रवेश करते हैं और जरासन्ध के सामने आते हैं, जो ब्राह्मण मानकर उनका सत्कार करता है पर सन्देह करता है; वे कहते हैं कि वे शत्रु का आतिथ्य स्वीकार नहीं करते।
summary.te: ఐదు కొండలు కాపాడే సమృద్ధమైన మగధ నగరాన్ని శ్రీకృష్ణుడు వర్ణిస్తాడు. ముగ్గురూ నగరపు పవిత్ర భేరీలను పగలగొట్టి నిషిద్ధ మార్గంలో ప్రవేశించి జరాసంధుని ఎదుట నిలుస్తారు; బ్రాహ్మణులుగా సత్కరించినా అతడు సందేహిస్తాడు; శత్రువు ఆతిథ్యం స్వీకరించమని వారు చెబుతారు.
summary.ta: ஐந்து மலைகள் காக்கும் செழிப்பான மகத நகரை ஸ்ரீகிருஷ்ணர் வர்ணிக்கிறார். மூவரும் நகரின் புனித முரசுகளை உடைத்து, தடுக்கப்பட்ட வழியாக நுழைந்து ஜராஸந்தன் முன் தோன்றுகிறார்கள்; அந்தணர்களாக மதித்தாலும் அவன் ஐயுறுகிறான்; பகைவனின் விருந்தோம்பலை ஏற்பதில்லை என்று அவர்கள் சொல்கிறார்கள்.
summary.ml: അഞ്ചു മലകൾ കാക്കുന്ന മഗധത്തിലെ സമ്പന്നനഗരത്തെ കൃഷ്ണൻ വിവരിക്കുന്നു. മൂവരും നഗരത്തിലെ പുണ്യഭേരികൾ തകർത്ത്, വിലക്കപ്പെട്ട വഴിയിലൂടെ പ്രവേശിച്ച് ജരാസന്ധന്റെ മുൻപിൽ എത്തുന്നു; അദ്ദേഹം ബ്രാഹ്മണരായി ബഹുമാനിക്കുന്നുവെങ്കിലും സംശയിക്കുന്നു; ശത്രുവിൽ നിന്ന് ആതിഥ്യം സ്വീകരിക്കില്ലെന്ന് അവർ പ്രഖ്യാപിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 2.19; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Apr 19 2006

verses.text: वासुदेव उवाच

meaning.en: Vasudeva said:

verses.text:
एष पार्थ महान्स्वादुः पशुमान्नित्यमम्बुमान् ।
निरामयः सुवेश्माढ्यो निवेशो मागधः शुभः ॥

meaning.en: This, Partha, is the great, pleasant and lovely land of Magadha, rich in cattle and always in water, free of disease and full of fine houses.

verses.text:
वैहारो विपुलः शैलो वराहो वृषभस्तथा ।
तथैवर्षिगिरिस्तात शुभाश्चैत्यकपञ्चमाः ॥

meaning.en: The hills Vaihara, Vipula, Varaha, Vrishabha and Rishigiri, my dear, these lovely ones, with Chaityaka the fifth,

verses.text:
एते पञ्च महाशृङ्गाः पर्वताः शीतलद्रुमाः ।
रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य संहताङ्गा गिरिव्रजम् ॥

meaning.en: are five great-peaked mountains with cool trees; joined together, with their limbs interlocked, they seem to guard Girivraja.

verses.text:
पुष्पवेष्टितशाखाग्रैर्गन्धवद्भिर्मनोरमैः ।
निगूढा इव लोध्राणां वनैः कामिजनप्रियैः ॥

meaning.en: Their branch tips wrapped in flowers, fragrant and charming, they seem hidden by woods of lodhra trees that lovers delight in.

verses.text:
शूद्रायां गौतमो यत्र महात्मा संशितव्रतः ।
औशीनर्यामजनयत्काक्षीवादीन्सुतानृषिः ॥

meaning.en: Here the great-souled Gautama, of strict vows, begot on an Aushinari Shudra woman sons such as Kakshivat.

verses.text:
गौतमः क्षयणादस्मादथासौ तत्र वेश्मनि ।
भजते मागधं वंशं स नृपाणामनुग्रहात् ॥

meaning.en: From that home Gautama, by the kings' favor, still serves the Magadha line in that house.

verses.text:
अङ्गवङ्गादयश्चैव राजानः सुमहाबलाः ।
गौतमक्षयमभ्येत्य रमन्ते स्म पुरार्जुन ॥

meaning.en: Kings of great strength, Anga, Vanga and others, in former times came to Gautama's dwelling and took delight, Arjuna.

verses.text:
वनराजीस्तु पश्येमाः प्रियालानां मनोरमाः ।
लोध्राणां च शुभाः पार्थ गौतमौकःसमीपजाः ॥

meaning.en: See these lovely rows of forest, of priyala and lodhra trees, Partha, that grow near Gautama's home.

verses.text:
अर्बुदः शक्रवापी च पन्नगौ शत्रुतापनौ ।
स्वस्तिकस्यालयश्चात्र मणिनागस्य चोत्तमः ॥

meaning.en: Here are Arbuda and Shakravapi, two serpents, tormentors of foes, and the finest dwelling of Svastika and of Maninaga.

verses.text:
अपरिहार्या मेघानां मागधेयं मणेः कृते ।
कौशिको मणिमांश्चैव ववृधाते ह्यनुग्रहम् ॥

meaning.en: Magadha is never to be harmed by clouds, because of the jewel; Kaushika and Maniman increased this favor.

verses.text:
अर्थसिद्धिं त्वनपगां जरासंधोऽभिमन्यते ।
वयमासादने तस्य दर्पमद्य निहन्म हि ॥

meaning.en: Jarasandha thinks his success is unfailing; when we reach him today, we shall crush his pride.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततः सर्वे भ्रातरो विपुलौजसः ।
वार्ष्णेयः पाण्डवेयौ च प्रतस्थुर्मागधं पुरम् ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, all those brothers of vast vigor, the Vrishni and the two Pandavas, went on toward the city of Magadha.

verses.text:
तुष्टपुष्टजनोपेतं चातुर्वर्ण्यजनाकुलम् ।
स्फीतोत्सवमनाधृष्यमासेदुश्च गिरिव्रजम् ॥

meaning.en: They reached Girivraja, full of contented, well-fed people and crowded with folk of the four classes, rich with festivals and hard to assail.

verses.text:
तेऽथ द्वारमनासाद्य पुरस्य गिरिमुच्छ्रितम् ।
बार्हद्रथैः पूज्यमानं तथा नगरवासिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Not going to the city gate, they came to the lofty mountain peak revered by the people of Brihadratha's line and by the townsmen,

verses.text:
यत्र माषादमृषभमाससाद बृहद्रथः ।
तं हत्वा माषनालाश्च तिस्रो भेरीरकारयत् ॥

meaning.en: where Brihadratha had met the bull-like Mashada, a man-eating demon; he killed him and had three drums made, with stalks of bean-plant frames.

verses.text:
आनह्य चर्मणा तेन स्थापयामास स्वे पुरे ।
यत्र ताः प्राणदन्भेर्यो दिव्यपुष्पावचूर्णिताः ॥

meaning.en: He covered them with that hide and set them up in his city; those drums sounded, strewn with heavenly flowers.

verses.text:
मागधानां सुरुचिरं चैत्यकान्तं समाद्रवन् ।
शिरसीव जिघांसन्तो जरासंधजिघांसवः ॥

meaning.en: They rushed upon the lovely Chaityaka peak of the Magadhas, as though to strike Jarasandha on the head, wishing to slay Jarasandha.

verses.text:
स्थिरं सुविपुलं शृङ्गं सुमहान्तं पुरातनम् ।
अर्चितं माल्यदामैश्च सततं सुप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥

meaning.en: That firm, vast, great, ancient peak, ever honored with garlands and well set,

verses.text:
विपुलैर्बाहुभिर्वीरास्तेऽभिहत्याभ्यपातयन् ।
ततस्ते मागधं दृष्ट्वा पुरं प्रविविशुस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: the heroes struck with their broad arms and brought crashing down. Then, seeing Magadha's city, they entered it.

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु जरासंधं समर्चयन् ।
पर्यग्नि कुर्वंश्च नृपं द्विरदस्थं पुरोहिताः ॥

meaning.en: At that very time the priests were honoring Jarasandha, carrying fire around the king as he sat on an elephant.

verses.text:
स्नातकव्रतिनस्ते तु बाहुशस्त्रा निरायुधाः ।
युयुत्सवः प्रविविशुर्जरासंधेन भारत ॥

meaning.en: Those snataka vow-keepers, with only their arms as weapons, unarmed, eager to fight, entered, O Bharata, against Jarasandha.

verses.text:
भक्ष्यमाल्यापणानां च ददृशुः श्रियमुत्तमाम् ।
स्फीतां सर्वगुणोपेतां सर्वकामसमृद्धिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: They saw the supreme splendor of the shops selling food and garlands, rich, endowed with every good thing and bringing every desire to fulfillment.

verses.text:
तां तु दृष्ट्वा समृद्धिं ते वीथ्यां तस्यां नरोत्तमाः ।
राजमार्गेण गच्छन्तः कृष्णभीमधनंजयाः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that prosperity in that street, the best of men, Krishna, Bhima and Dhananjaya, went along the king's road.

verses.text:
बलाद्गृहीत्वा माल्यानि मालाकारान्महाबलाः ।
विरागवसनाः सर्वे स्रग्विणो मृष्टकुण्डलाः ॥

meaning.en: Mighty ones, they seized garlands by force from the garland-makers, all in dyed robes, wreathed and with polished earrings,

verses.text:
निवेशनमथाजग्मुर्जरासंधस्य धीमतः ।
गोवासमिव वीक्षन्तः सिंहा हैमवता यथा ॥

meaning.en: and so came to the house of the wise Jarasandha, looking about like lions of the Himalaya at a cowpen.

verses.text:
शैलस्तम्भनिभास्तेषां चन्दनागुरुभूषिताः ।
अशोभन्त महाराज बाहवो बाहुशालिनाम् ॥

meaning.en: Their arms, like pillars of rock and adorned with sandal and aloe, shone, O great king, those arms of men with mighty arms.

verses.text:
तान्दृष्ट्वा द्विरदप्रख्याञ्शालस्कन्धानिवोद्गतान् ।
व्यूढोरस्कान्मागधानां विस्मयः समजायत ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them, tall as elephants, rising like sal trunks, broad-chested, the Magadhas were astonished.

verses.text:
ते त्वतीत्य जनाकीर्णास्तिस्रः कक्ष्या नरर्षभाः ।
अहंकारेण राजानमुपतस्थुर्महाबलाः ॥

meaning.en: The bulls among men, mighty and proud, passed through three crowded courtyards and approached the king.

verses.text:
तान्पाद्यमधुपर्कार्हान्मानार्हान्सत्कृतिं गतान् ।
प्रत्युत्थाय जरासंध उपतस्थे यथाविधि ॥

meaning.en: Jarasandha rose and received them duly, they who deserved foot-water, honey-milk and honor, and were now honored.

verses.text:
उवाच चैतान्राजासौ स्वागतं वोऽस्त्विति प्रभुः ।
तस्य ह्येतद्व्रतं राजन्बभूव भुवि विश्रुतम् ॥

meaning.en: The king said to them, "Welcome to you," for this was his well-known vow in the world, O king.

verses.text:
स्नातकान्ब्राह्मणान्प्राप्ताञ्श्रुत्वा स समितिंजयः ।
अप्यर्धरात्रे नृपतिः प्रत्युद्गच्छति भारत ॥

meaning.en: Hearing that snataka Brahmins had come, the conqueror of assemblies went out to meet them even at midnight, Bharata.

verses.text:
तांस्त्वपूर्वेण वेषेण दृष्ट्वा नृपतिसत्तमः ।
उपतस्थे जरासंधो विस्मितश्चाभवत्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them in strange dress, the best of kings stood before them and was astonished.

verses.text:
ते तु दृष्ट्वैव राजानं जरासंधं नरर्षभाः ।
इदमूचुरमित्रघ्नाः सर्वे भरतसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: But the bulls among men, slayers of enemies, the moment they saw King Jarasandha, said this, best of the Bharatas:

verses.text:
स्वस्त्यस्तु कुशलं राजन्निति सर्वे व्यवस्थिताः ।
तं नृपं नृपशार्दूल विप्रैक्षन्त परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: "May there be good and welfare, O king," all said, as they stood there. And they looked at the king, and at one another, tiger among kings.

verses.text:
तानब्रवीज्जरासंधस्तदा यादवपाण्डवान् ।
आस्यतामिति राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणच्छद्मसंवृतान् ॥

meaning.en: Then Jarasandha said to those Yadava and Pandava men, disguised as Brahmins, "Please be seated."

verses.text:
अथोपविविशुः सर्वे त्रयस्ते पुरुषर्षभाः ।
संप्रदीप्तास्त्रयो लक्ष्म्या महाध्वर इवाग्नयः ॥

meaning.en: Then all three bulls among men sat down, blazing with splendor, like three fires at a great sacrifice.

verses.text:
तानुवाच जरासंधः सत्यसंधो नराधिपः ।
विगर्हमाणः कौरव्य वेषग्रहणकारणात् ॥

meaning.en: The truthful king Jarasandha, O Kaurava, spoke to them, finding fault with the garb they had taken:

verses.text:
न स्नातकव्रता विप्रा बहिर्माल्यानुलेपनाः ।
भवन्तीति नृलोकेऽस्मिन्विदितं मम सर्वशः ॥

meaning.en: "I know well in this world of men that snataka Brahmins do not wear garlands and unguents outside the house.

verses.text:
ते यूयं पुष्पवन्तश्च भुजैर्ज्याघातलक्षणैः ।
बिभ्रतः क्षात्रमोजश्च ब्राह्मण्यं प्रतिजानथ ॥

meaning.en: "You are flower-wreathed, your arms bear the marks of the bowstring, and, bearing a Kshatriya's vigor, you claim to be Brahmins.

verses.text:
एवं विरागवसना बहिर्माल्यानुलेपनाः ।
सत्यं वदत के यूयं सत्यं राजसु शोभते ॥

meaning.en: "So, in dyed robes, wearing garlands and unguent outside, tell me the truth: who are you? Truth is what shines among kings.

verses.text:
चैत्यकं च गिरेः शृङ्गं भित्त्वा किमिव सद्म नः ।
अद्वारेण प्रविष्टाः स्थ निर्भया राजकिल्बिषात् ॥

meaning.en: "Why did you break the Chaityaka peak of the mountain and enter our house by no door, without fear of the king's wrath?

verses.text:
कर्म चैतद्विलिङ्गस्य किं वाद्य प्रसमीक्षितम् ।
वदध्वं वाचि वीर्यं च ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः ॥

meaning.en: "This is the act of men in false garb; what did you intend today? Tell me, for a Brahmin especially has power in speech.

verses.text:
एवं च मामुपस्थाय कस्माच्च विधिनार्हणाम् ।
प्रणीतां नो न गृह्णीत कार्यं किं चास्मदागमे ॥

meaning.en: "And having come to me, why do you not accept the proper honor we offered you? What is the purpose of your coming?"

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः प्रत्युवाच महामनाः ।
स्निग्धगम्भीरया वाचा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed, the great-minded Krishna, skilled in speech, replied in a calm and deep voice.

verses.text:
स्नातकव्रतिनो राजन्ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया विशः ।
विशेषनियमाश्चैषामविशेषाश्च सन्त्युत ॥

meaning.en: "King, snataka vow-keepers may be Brahmins, Kshatriyas or Vaishyas; they have special rules and also ordinary ones.

verses.text:
विशेषवांश्च सततं क्षत्रियः श्रियमर्छति ।
पुष्पवत्सु ध्रुवा श्रीश्च पुष्पवन्तस्ततो वयम् ॥

meaning.en: "A Kshatriya who keeps special rules always earns fortune; fortune stays firm with those who are flowery, and so we wear flowers.

verses.text:
क्षत्रियो बाहुवीर्यस्तु न तथा वाक्यवीर्यवान् ।
अप्रगल्भं वचस्तस्य तस्माद्बार्हद्रथे स्मृतम् ॥

meaning.en: "A Kshatriya's power is in his arms, not in his speech in the same way; his speech is not bold; thus it is told in Brihadratha's son's case.

verses.text:
स्ववीर्यं क्षत्रियाणां च बाह्वोर्धाता न्यवेशयत् ।
तद्दिदृक्षसि चेद्राजन्द्रष्टास्यद्य न संशयः ॥

meaning.en: "The Creator placed the Kshatriyas' strength in their arms; if you wish to see it, king, you will see it today, without doubt.

verses.text:
अद्वारेण रिपोर्गेहं द्वारेण सुहृदो गृहम् ।
प्रविशन्ति सदा सन्तो द्वारं नो वर्जितं ततः ॥

meaning.en: "Good men always enter an enemy's house by a no-door and a friend's house by a door; so we avoided the door.

verses.text:
कार्यवन्तो गृहानेत्य शत्रुतो नार्हणां वयम् ।
प्रतिगृह्णीम तद्विद्धि एतन्नः शाश्वतं व्रतम् ॥

meaning.en: "Having come to a house on business, we do not take honor from an enemy; know that this is our everlasting vow."
